boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on walkable corridors around Harvard Square, each paired with one directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Browse an Independent Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue at Plympton Street
cards.notes: Walk east along Massachusetts Avenue to browse new, used, and bargain books at this independently run Cambridge bookseller.
cards.short_summary: A book-focused stop three blocks east of Harvard Square station.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Book Store identifies its location as 1256 Massachusetts Avenue and describes itself as a locally owned, independently run Cambridge bookstore founded in 1932.
cards.access_notes: The store's official directions page lists regular hours; check it before visiting because schedules can change.

cards.title: Find the Sidewalk Marquee
cards.subtitle: Brattle Street, one block from Harvard station
cards.notes: Follow Brattle Street to the poster case and marquee, then consult the theater calendar before choosing a repertory-film screening.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable cinema entrance anchors this Brattle Street block.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brattle Theatre states that it operates in Brattle Hall at 40 Brattle Street, one block from the Harvard Square MBTA stop, with its entrance marked by a poster case and marquee.
cards.access_notes: Public entry is tied to scheduled screenings and events; consult the official calendar and ticket information.

cards.title: Step Into a Poetry-Only Bookshop
cards.subtitle: Plympton Street off Massachusetts Avenue
cards.notes: Turn onto Plympton Street and browse a compact shop devoted solely to poetry; verify its limited weekly opening days first.
cards.short_summary: A specialized poetry collection gives this side street a clear literary reason to turn off Mass. Ave.
cards.evidence_claim: Grolier Poetry Book Shop says it is dedicated solely to poetry books and lists its shop at 6 Plympton Street in Cambridge.
cards.access_notes: The official site currently lists Wednesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–7 p.m., and notes closures on most federal holidays.

cards.title: Check the Community-Class Calendar
cards.subtitle: Brattle Street at 42 and 56 Brattle
cards.notes: Continue along Brattle Street and scan CCAE’s calendar for a public class or event held in one of its two historic properties.
cards.short_summary: Classes and events animate two neighboring Brattle Street properties.
cards.evidence_claim: Cambridge Center for Adult Education describes itself as a nonprofit founded in 1871, with classroom locations at 42 and 56 Brattle Street in Harvard Square.
cards.access_notes: Building access generally follows registered classes, events, and posted office hours; consult the current calendar.

cards.entity_name: Longfellow House–Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site
cards.title: Walk Through a Historic Garden
cards.subtitle: Brattle Street at 105 Brattle
cards.notes: Follow Brattle Street west to explore the year-round grounds, then take a seasonal house tour if the current schedule permits.
cards.short_summary: A preserved Georgian house and garden extend the Brattle Street walk into national history.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service places the site at 105 Brattle Street, states that its grounds are open year-round from dawn to dusk, and offers seasonal guided house tours.
cards.source_title: Basic Information – Longfellow House-Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site
cards.access_notes: Grounds are open dawn to dusk. House hours vary seasonally, and winter tours may require an appointment.

cards.title: Descend to a Comics Shop
cards.subtitle: Mount Auburn Street at 99 Mount Auburn
cards.notes: Take Mount Auburn Street to the downstairs storefront and browse its comics, toys, and T-shirts during posted shop hours.
cards.short_summary: A below-street-level comics store supplies a distinct stop on Mount Auburn Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Million Year Picnic lists its downstairs store at 99 Mount Auburn Street and identifies its merchandise as comics, toys, and T-shirts.
cards.source_title: The Million Year Picnic | About Us
cards.access_notes: The official page currently lists daily hours of 11 a.m.–7 p.m.; confirm before setting out.

cards.title: Use a Public Study Room
cards.subtitle: Broadway at 449 Broadway
cards.notes: Head east on Broadway to use Wi-Fi, study rooms, computers, or the collections inside the linked historic and glass library wings.
cards.short_summary: Public study resources and contrasting architecture reward the walk east on Broadway.
cards.evidence_claim: Cambridge Public Library lists the Main Library at 449 Broadway and identifies features including Wi-Fi, study rooms, computers, collections, and two architecturally distinct wings.
cards.access_notes: The city page lists current daily hours and service features; some rooms or equipment may have separate use rules.

cards.title: Browse the Campus Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue at 1400 Massachusetts
cards.notes: Walk the Massachusetts Avenue frontage to browse textbooks, general books, Harvard apparel, and the store’s event offerings.
cards.short_summary: The cooperatively owned campus bookstore marks a prominent Mass. Ave. retail block.
cards.evidence_claim: The COOP lists its Harvard Square store at 1400 Massachusetts Avenue; Harvard describes it as a cooperatively owned bookstore carrying textbooks, bestsellers, and Harvard apparel.
cards.access_notes: The COOP's official contact page provides current store hours; browsing is public during open hours.

cards.title: Trace the Common’s Monuments
cards.subtitle: Garden Street between Massachusetts Avenue and Waterhouse Street
cards.notes: Circle the Garden Street edge, then use the park paths to find lawns, historic monuments, and the Alexander W. Kemp Playground.
cards.short_summary: A 16-acre civic landscape opens immediately beyond Harvard Square’s commercial blocks.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cambridge identifies Cambridge Common as a 16-acre city park and National Historic Landmark bordered by Massachusetts Avenue, Garden Street, and Waterhouse Street, with paths, lawns, monuments, and a playground.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor municipal park; observe posted field, playground, and event rules during your visit.

cards.title: See the Restored Newsstand
cards.subtitle: Harvard Square plaza beside Massachusetts Avenue
cards.notes: Cross the plaza to inspect the restored former newsstand, pick up visitor information, and check its rotating program or exhibit.
cards.short_summary: The renewed landmark turns Harvard Square’s central plaza into a small arts-and-information stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Cambridge KiOSK describes the restored former Out of Town News building as a Harvard Square public space offering free programming, visitor information, exhibits, and gathering space.
cards.access_notes: Programs are free, but building and event hours vary; check the KiOSK's current schedule before visiting.
